seo_title: Cost of Living in Fethiye 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Fethiye per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: A resort on Turkey's turquoise coast: visa-free entry, a mild Mediterranean climate, the famous Ölüdeniz and yacht-filled bays. Cheaper than Bodrum and more laid-back; in winter the resort life quiets down.
pros: A turquoise sea and the famous Ölüdeniz
Cheaper and more laid-back than Bodrum
A Russian-speaking community and familiar services
cons: Resort life winds down in winter
Some coastal districts are closed to the tourist residence permit
No airport of its own — the nearest is in Dalaman

visa_steps.title: Visa-free entry
visa_steps.description: Russian citizens don't need a visa for short trips — the stamp is issued at the border.

visa_steps.title: Check the district
visa_steps.description: Before renting, make sure the neighbourhood is open for issuing residence permits to foreigners.

faq.question: Do Russians need a visa for Fethiye?
faq.answer: No, you don't need a visa for short trips. For long-term living you apply for a residence permit (ikamet).

faq.question: How much does it cost to live in Fethiye?
faq.answer: Cheaper and more laid-back than Bodrum. See the exact budget in the calculator above.

faq.question: Which language is spoken in Fethiye?
faq.answer: Turkish; English is common in tourist areas, and you'll hear Russian too.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Fethiye?
faq.answer: Russian cards don't work. You'll need cash lira and a card from a foreign or Turkish bank.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Fethiye?
faq.answer: Mediterranean: hot, dry summers and mild, rainy winters.

faq.question: How do I get to Fethiye?
faq.answer: The nearest airport is Dalaman, about an hour's drive; in summer there are direct flights from Russia.

reviews.text: Fethiye means a turquoise sea and mountains, quieter and cheaper than Bodrum. The resort goes quiet in winter, and I had to wrestle with the residence permit because of the closed districts.
We moved for Ölüdeniz and the climate. It's beautiful in summer but crowded. There are plenty of Russian speakers, and settling in went smoothly.
